summary: Extends Mobile IPv4 to support mobile networks, where a Mobile Router moves one or more subnets together and its Home Agent keeps them reachable. The Mobile Router hides the movement from nodes behind it, which need no mobility support. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: On a bus with many travelers, one device handles the connection for all of them. This paper lets a whole moving group keep one address while the bus travels.

questions: what is nemo for mobile ipv4
what is the mobile network extension type
subtitle: How a Mobile IPv4 router can carry a whole moving subnet with it and keep every device behind it reachable.

tldr.problem: Mobile IPv4 handles single moving hosts, but a bus, train or personal network moves a whole subnet at once, and the Home Agent had no way to register which prefixes a Mobile Router serves or check that it may.
tldr.mechanism: Two new extensions (Mobile Network Request and Mobile Network Acknowledgement) ride on the normal Registration Request and Reply, so the Home Agent can authorize the prefixes and tunnel their traffic to the Mobile Router.
tldr.outcome: Devices behind the Mobile Router need no mobility software and never see its address change. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has since been updated by RFC 6626.

today: RFC 5177 is a Proposed Standard and has been updated by RFC 6626. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Moving a Whole Network
sections.content:
RFC 5177 extends Mobile IPv4 for cases where groups of hosts and routers move together as a whole. All of them must still be able to run Internet applications and be reachable from the Internet. The RFC calls its result NEMOv4.

The moving group is a Mobile Network. One example in the text is a PDA and a camera linked by Bluetooth, where the PDA acts as the Mobile Router and the camera as a Local Fixed Node. Laptops used by passengers in a bus, train, ship or plane also count, as long as they move together.
sections.eli5: Some things travel as a group, like a bus full of people with phones. This paper lets the whole group keep working on the Internet while it moves.

sections.title: What the Design Must Achieve
sections.content:
Mobile IPv4 in RFC 3344 allowed Mobile Networks through static configuration or a routing protocol, but gave no way to explicitly register them. A solution has to let the Home Agent confirm that a Mobile Router claiming a prefix is authorized to do so, and should show the prefixes in the messages to help debugging.

  • A Mobile Router can work in explicit mode (it lists its prefixes) or implicit mode (the Home Agent learns them another way, such as a AAA server, pre-configuration or a routing protocol).
  • Unchanged ('legacy') Foreign Agents should work.
  • Fixed nodes, Mobile Nodes or Mobile Routers may sit on the Mobile Network.
  • Local Fixed Nodes run their sessions without a Mobile IP stack, because the Mobile Router hides changes of Care-of Address.
sections.eli5: The helper on the bus has to prove it is allowed to speak for the kids. The kids themselves should not need any special gadgets.

sections.title: The Mobile Network Extensions
sections.content:
Both extensions use Type 148 (Mobile Network Extension) in Type-Length-Value form, and a Sub-Type tells them apart.

The Mobile Network Request (Sub-Type 0, Length 6) goes in a Registration Request in explicit mode. Each one carries a Prefix Length and a 32-bit Prefix, and a request may hold zero, one or several of them, one per prefix.

The Mobile Network Acknowledgement (Length 8) goes in the Registration Reply. Sub-Type 1 is the explicit mode acknowledgement and 2 the implicit one. It adds a Code and a Reserved field (sent as zero, ignored on reception). A successful reply MUST contain at least one acknowledgement, so the Mobile Router knows its request was processed and not skipped.

The acknowledgement Code is 0 for success, 1 for an invalid prefix length, 2 when the Mobile Router is not authorized for the prefix and 3 when forwarding setup failed.
sections.eli5: The helper adds a note to its normal letter saying which streets it speaks for. The post office adds a note back saying yes or no for each street.

sections.title: Registration and Tunnels
sections.content:
The Mobile Router registers its Care-of Address with the Home Agent in a Registration Request and gets a Reply, which sets up a tunnel between them. The Mobile Router SHOULD set the T bit to 1 in every Registration Request so that traffic goes through a reverse tunnel. Without it, ingress filtering in visited networks would hit all traffic from the Mobile Network. After a successful reply it checks the acknowledgements, creates the tunnel if reverse tunneling was used and sets a default route through the tunnel or the egress interface.

In explicit mode the Home Agent checks that the prefix information is valid, ensures the prefixes are authorized for that Mobile Router, creates the tunnel if needed, routes the prefixes through it, propagates the routes if necessary and replies. Authorization is a lookup in its Prefix Table that must pair the Mobile Router's Home Address with the prefix. In implicit mode the Home Agent does the tunnel, route, propagation and reply steps once the registration succeeds. Subnet routes via the tunnel that are not in the extensions are removed.

Deregistration uses a request with lifetime zero and no Mobile Network Request extensions. The Home Agent then removes the tunnel and its routes and ignores any Mobile Network extensions.
sections.eli5: The helper tells the post office where it is and which streets it covers. The post office checks its list, then builds a private pipe to the helper for those streets' mail.

sections.title: Forwarding and Nesting
sections.content:
If the Mobile Router registered through a Foreign Agent Care-of Address, the Home Agent MUST double-tunnel traffic for the Mobile Network: first to the Mobile Router's Home Address, then to the Care-of Address. In co-located Care-of Address mode the Home Agent SHOULD use only the outer tunnel. For packets coming back, the Home Agent de-encapsulates and routes them as normal IP, but MUST drop a packet whose source is not the Mobile Router's Care-of Address.

All traffic between the Mobile Network and its correspondents passes through the Home Agent, and route optimization is not covered. Multihoming for Mobile Routers is out of scope.

Nested mobility, where one Mobile Router attaches to another's network, is allowed with no limit on depth. The RFC warns that physical loops are neither detected nor solved, and that each level adds a tunnel header, which shrinks the usable MTU for applications that do not support MTU discovery.
sections.eli5: All mail still goes through the home post office first. If a bus rides on another bus, the mail gets wrapped in one more envelope for each bus, so it gets bulkier.

sections.title: Error Codes and Routing Protocols
sections.content:
A reply can carry two Code fields: the one in the Registration Reply header and the one inside the Mobile Network Acknowledgement. IANA assigned two header codes: 147 (HA_MOBNET_ERROR) and 148 (HA_MOBNET_DISALLOWED). On HA_MOBNET_DISALLOWED the Mobile Router MUST stop sending Mobile Network prefix extensions to that Home Agent. On HA_MOBNET_ERROR it MUST stop sending the prefixes named in the acknowledgement. A reply with no Mobile Network extensions means the Home Agent does not support Mobile Networks.

A dynamic routing protocol such as OSPF, BGP or RIP can also run between the Mobile Router and Home Agent. If a prefix is sent that way it SHOULD NOT also be in the Registration Request, and the Mobile Router SHOULD use implicit mode. It SHOULD NOT send routing updates in the foreign network, because the moving network's prefixes are topologically incorrect there.
sections.eli5: If the post office says no, the helper must stop asking for those streets. If the post office never heard of the idea, the helper knows not to try.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The Home Agent MUST verify that the Mobile Router is authorized for the prefixes before anchoring them, and MUST NOT set up forwarding without that authorization. The Mobile Router MUST be told when authorization fails.

All Registration Requests and replies MUST be authenticated with the MN-HA Authentication Extension from RFC 3344, and the Mobile Network extensions MUST come before it and be included in the authenticator calculation.

Against spoofing through the tunnel, the Mobile Router MUST drop packets from the Mobile Network whose source is not in that network, or equals its own address on any interface. The Home Agent MUST check the outer source is the Care-of Address and the inner source is a topologically correct Mobile Network address. If a routing protocol is used, its updates SHOULD be protected with IPsec ESP confidentiality.
sections.eli5: The post office must check the helper's pass before sending mail, and both sides check that nobody fakes a return address.
